title: Tenali and the King of Thieves

keywords: tenali and the king of thieves
full_text:
A notorious master burglar named Chora Raja (The King of Thieves) sent an insolent letter to Emperor Krishnadevaraya:
'Imperial King! Your palace guards are sleeping sheep, and your treasury locks are made of clay.
On the night of the full moon, I will break into the Royal Treasury Vault inside the innermost citadel, steal the Great Emerald of Vijayanagara, and leave a painted flower in its place!'

The King was outraged and doubled the palace guards. Three hundred armored soldiers surrounded the treasury, and the chief locksmith installed triple steel padlocks.
Yet the King remained anxious and called Tenali Raman.

Tenali smiled: 'Maharaj, a master thief does not break through walls guarded by spears; he walks through doors opened by greed. Let me prepare the trap inside the vault.'

Tenali had all the gold coins and emeralds removed from the central display table in the vault and locked in a secret subterranean safe.
In their place, in the center of the dark vault, Tenali placed an enormous, magnificent iron-bound chest made of seasoned teakwood. The chest lid was slightly ajar, revealing a glittering false diamond necklace resting on velvet.
Tenali himself climbed inside the chest, armed with a small copper horn and a net of strong hemp cord, pulling the lid down to leave a two-inch breathing crack.

At midnight, a subtle shadow slipped through the high ventilation skylight using a silk rope.
Chora Raja had bribed an outer groom to learn the guard patrol schedule!
Silently landing on the marble floor of the vault, the master thief chuckled at his easy entry.

Seeing the massive teakwood chest in the center of the room with the glittering necklace peeking out, Chora Raja’s eyes gleamed with greed.
He crept forward, lifted the heavy lid, and reached his hands inside to seize the necklace!

Instantly, two powerful hands shot out from the darkness inside the chest, grabbing Chora Raja’s wrists with an iron grip!
Before the stunned burglar could draw his dagger, Tenali threw the heavy hemp net over his head and blew a deafening blast on his copper horn:
*‘HONK-TOOT-TOOT!’*

Fifty royal guards burst into the vault with torches and spears!
Chora Raja was pinned to the floor, completely tangled in the net!

When the thief looked into the chest and saw Tenali Raman grinning back at him, he gasped in disbelief:
'Who art thou that sleeps inside a treasure chest?'
Tenali laughed, climbing out of the box:
'I am the keeper of greed's mousetrap!
Thou didst boast that no lock could keep thee out, but thou didst forget that a thief’s own greed locks him in from the inside!'

The King rewarded Tenali with the recovered emerald, and Chora Raja was imprisoned, ending the reign of the boastful burglar.
moral: Audacious criminals who boast that no lock can hold them are trapped by their own irresistible greed.
